title: Driveshaft Specifications
introduction:
The driveshaft carries rotation from the transmission to the rear differential, with joints accommodating the working angles along that route. I read these specifications like a route map: identify the joint first, then match the engine and transmission. A nearby row is not a substitute just because its number looks friendly.

Use the material table for grease identification, the geometry table for runout and joint-angle specifications, and the torque table for the named fastener or flange arrangement. Joint angles apply at curb ride height. This reference supplies values, not the measurement setup, removal sequence or fastener-reuse rules needed for a service procedure.

edits.text: Driveshaft Lubricants, Fluids, Sealers and Adhesives
edits.why: Match the grease by its product identification and specification. In the following geometry table, distinguish runout—the variation in a surface's path as it rotates—from joint angle. Select each angle by joint location, engine and transmission, retaining the rear-differential rows' specific inclusions and exclusions. The listed angles apply at curb ride height; this table does not establish how to set up or perform the measurements.

Identify the actual attachment before selecting its row, especially the front driveshaft flange arrangements. Keep the chosen value under its printed Nm, lb-ft or lb-in heading. A dash supplies no value in that unit; the table also does not authorize fastener reuse or establish a tightening sequence.
